notes:
Summary: Enterprise healthcare SaaS, must keep PHI in EU region. Strong interest in Redwood Private (VPC) to avoid egress of sensitive data. Primary ask: private network connectivity (AWS PrivateLink or VPC peering), strict egress controls, and ability to allowlist specific Redwood IPs. They require KMS BYOK for model inference logs and full audit log delivery to Splunk.

Key quote from CTO: "We cannot accept any outbound traffic to public endpoints without firewall rules and egress control — every request must be mappable to an audit path."

Tone: pragmatic, security-first. Buying group includes infosec, platform, legal, and procurement. They are comparing Redwood Private vs building internal serving on EC2/GKE. Cost sensitivity: moderate — will pay premium for certainties around compliance and SLA.

Ask for next call: come back with reference network diagrams, expected CIDR ranges for endpoints, KMS integration flow (bring-your-own-key), and audit log retention/export options.

technical_requirements: Private connectivity: prefer AWS PrivateLink; willing to evaluate VPC peering for lower latency
IP allowlist: need static egress IPs for outbound callbacks and audit exports
Firewall rules: deny all outbound except approved Redwood endpoints and Splunk ingestion
Egress controls: NAT + explicit routing to prevent accidental internet egress
KMS: BYOK required for storing request logs and KV cache dump — must integrate with customer AWS KMS/HSM
Audit logging: forward inference logs (redacted PHI) to customer SIEM (Splunk) and keep immutable retention for 3 years
Network sizing: support for sustained 100 req/s with 50ms p95 latency target for chat assistant
DNS: private hosted zone or split-horizon DNS to resolve Redwood private endpoints
TLS: mutual TLS optional for service-to-service calls
Failover: cross-region fallback to EU-secondary region; fallbacks must respect data residency and not replicate logs outside EU

Week 3 — Small traffic experiment (10r/s) with audit logging to Splunk; validate latency and egress rules
Week 4 — Scale test to 100r/s, run resilience tests and failover scenarios; handoff to CSM for onboarding
